verdict.rationale: Fastmail publishes a developer page documenting its public JMAP API. It covers a session endpoint at api.fastmail.com, API-token, OAuth or Bearer auth, CORS-enabled APIs, and the IETF RFCs as the full specification. Batched methodCalls let a client query, fetch and send in one request, which is a documented public API an agent can drive. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of driving Fastmail via the API, and a downloadable machine-readable spec (OpenAPI paths and llms.txt return 404, though JMAP's RFCs serve as the spec).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The JMAP session resource can be found at https://api.fastmail.com/jmap/session
POST a `methodCalls` array. Query, fetch, and send, all in one HTTP request.
Standard OAuth 2.0 or Bearer tokens. No custom auth protocol to implement.
No patents. No fees. Fully documented.
